_comment: An amendment to G.4, written 2026-10-18. It does not replace
chip/PREREGISTRATION.json and it does not change a byte of it. That
file is recorded here by hash and stays on disk as it was frozen on
31 August, and preregister.py --freeze-check still holds it there.
The research design was read cold on 8 September and four findings
came out of that audit. Four more gaps were found on 23 September and
one on 18 October. The four decisions of 3 October are five items
below, the three of 18 October are three more, and the one about
which count is a reading dates from 23 September, when the firmware
began starting every selection twice. No die existed for any of them.
preregister.py --amendment holds this file to the frozen one: every
item quotes the frozen text it amends, and the gate fails if the quote
and the frozen file part company.
not_a_preregistration_why: PREREGISTRATION.json was frozen on 31 August before any of this was
known, and that is what makes it a preregistration. This file was
written after an audit of that plan, with the audit's numbers in hand.
No die had been read and nothing had been measured, so none of it can
have been fitted to data, but it is still a set of decisions taken
late, and it must never be cited as though it carried the frozen
file's weight. The paper says so in the same words.

amends.frozen_text: M1 across three arms, M2 across three arms, M4 once. Seven tests.
now: Two primary tests, M1 on Arm A and M4. Holm runs over those two
only, so the smaller p is tested at 0.025 and the other at 0.05 if
the first passed. M1 on Arms B and C and M2 on all three arms are
secondary: computed, reported, and carrying no claim of their own.
why: Under the frozen family of seven the first Holm level is 0.05/7,
0.007143, and a perfect M1 on Arm A, six scored pairs all called
right, has p = 0.015625. The leakage claim would be reported false
on exactly the result it predicts. That is the audit's finding 1.
With two primaries six of six passes, and five of five, p =
0.03125, can still pass second.
gives_up: M2, and M1 on Arms B and C, no longer carry a claim. Arm B near
chance and Arm B not repeating become reported results and stop
being tests that have to come out as nulls, which is most of the
audit's finding 3.

amends.frozen_text: If Arm A's predictable-bit count is not above chance with the Holm-corrected family below 0.05 across the declared comparisons, the leakage claim fails and the paper says so.
now: The test is the exact one-sided binomial on Arm A's scored pairs:
with n pairs not abstaining and k of them called right, p is the
chance of k or more right out of n at one half each. The leakage
claim fails unless p clears the level Holm gives it.
why: The frozen text names a correction and no test. A binomial over
one die's pairs and one pooled over dies are both defensible, and
the audit put the gap between them at two orders of magnitude in
power, so the choice had to be made while there was no data.
gives_up: the pooled reading, which would have more power with more dies.
M1 is a test on one die, see the item named die.

amends.frozen_text: of the 8 pairs in an arm, the number whose measured sign matches the sign predicted from the public design database before silicon, counting only non-abstaining pairs.
now: M1 and M4 are tested on the first die read, and on no other. Which
die that is goes into the archive with its first reading, before
anything is computed on it. Every other die is reported with the
same numbers and tests nothing.
why: Both are tests on one die and the frozen text never says which.
M2 needs three dies, so more than one is the plan, and a die chosen
after reading them all is a result chosen.
gives_up: whatever power later dies would have added to M1 and M4. They stay
one die's tests however many come in.

amends.frozen_text: Spearman correlation of the 16 per-ring mean frequencies between every pair of dies, within an arm, at the nominal cell.
now: M2 is computed only if three or more dies have been read by
2027-09-30, and is reported as not run otherwise. The pairs of dies
are combined as the mean of the pairwise Spearman correlations, and
its p-value comes from shuffling each die's ring labels.
why: The frozen text names no die count and no way to combine D(D-1)/2
correlations that are not independent, so as written M2 cannot be
computed. That is the audit's finding 4. One devkit is one die.
gives_up: with one devkit M2 rests on other people's boards, and under three
dies it does not run at all.

amends.frozen_text: the standard deviation of the 16 Arm C mean frequencies at the nominal cell, divided by the same figure for Arm A on the same die.
now: M4 stays as frozen. One secondary is named before any data: Arm
C's spread inside its lower eight rings and inside its upper eight,
pooled, over Arm A's spread. The paper gives the two footprints,
Arm C 77 by 180 um around Arm A's 59 by 98.

halves.read_from: dualarm/src/armc_fix.tcl, where each ring's NAND sits
halves.pooled: the two sums of squares about each half's own mean, over fourteen degrees of freedom

why: Arm C's column is taller than Arm A's block, so a gradient up the
die adds more to Arm C's spread than to Arm A's, and that works
against the claim. That is the audit's finding 2. Lower and upper
mean below and above Arm A, by where the hook puts each ring and
not by ring number. Each half spans 33 um of height, where the
whole column spans 180 and Arm A 98.
gives_up: the primary number still carries the position term, and it works
against the claim. The secondary decides nothing.

amends.frozen_text: If Arm C's spread ratio is not below 1 with its confidence interval clear of 1, placement equalization did not suppress the layout term and the paper reports a null.
now: The interval comes from a permutation test, inverted, on the first
die read. M4 supports the claim only if the ratio is below 1 and
p(1) is at or under the level Holm gives M4, which is the interval
being clear of 1.

method.statistic: the sample standard deviation of Arm C's 16 ring means over Arm A's, the frozen M4
method.centring: each arm's 16 values less that arm's own median
method.test: for a ratio r, Arm C's centred values are divided by r and pooled with Arm A's, and the 32 are shuffled between the two arms, 16 and 16; p(r) is the share of shuffles, the observed split counted as one of them, whose ratio is at or under the observed one
method.generator: one random.Random(seed), shuffling the pooled indices in place again and again, Arm A's in ring order first, every order kept and used at every r
method.level: the level Holm gives M4 over the two primaries, 0.025 if its p(1) is the smaller of the two and 0.05 if M1 passed first
method.interval: every r whose p(r) is above that level, its upper end found by bisection on log r
method.decision: the ratio below 1 and p(1) at or under the level

why: The frozen text asks for an interval and names none. A ratio of two
standard deviations over sixteen values a side is where the
textbook F interval is least safe: it is exact only for normal
data, ring frequencies shaped by a layout need not be normal, and
with heavy tails it comes out too narrow, which makes passing
easier than it should be. A bootstrap over sixteen rings comes out
too narrow as well. The permutation test assumes only that the two
arms, centred, differ in scale and not in shape.
gives_up: a formula a reader can check with a table. This one needs the
script, the seed and a hundred thousand shuffles. And some power if
the frequencies do turn out normal: on normal arms of sixteen it
wants the ratio under about 0.56 to clear 0.025 where the F
interval wants 0.591.

amends.frozen_text: each read 20 times on every one of 48 oscillators
now: A reading is the count from the second of two starts on one
selection. The first start's count is kept beside it as
count_first and analysed on its own, as the first-start effect of
docs/phaseG_hazard.md. It never stands in for a reading, in M1 to
M4 or anywhere else.
why: Since 23 September the firmware starts every selection twice,
because the first run after a change of selection can read one
high, and the datasheet tells anyone measuring to do the same. The
frozen protocol was written when a reading was one start and has
no word for this. It is written down here as the firmware and the
datasheet have had it since that day.
gives_up: half the starts on a die go to something that is not a reading.

amends.frozen_text: ABBA within every cell: arm A, then B, then B, then A, then C twice in the same mirrored order. Sequential comparison drifts; a mirrored order cancels a linear drift over the cell.
now: Inside every cell each of the 20 repeats reads all 48 oscillators
once, in a fresh order drawn from a seeded generator. The seed and
a time stamp for every reading are recorded, as
firmware/measure_puf.py already does.
why: The bench firmware has read in this order since July and is
tested on it, and no script in the repository reads in the frozen
one. The
frozen sentence fixes the order of the arms and not of the sixteen
rings inside an arm, where an order that repeats would line ring
index up with any drift inside the block, and that is spread M4
would count. A random order keeps arm and ring from lining up with
time at all.
gives_up: the exact cancelling of a linear drift that a mirrored order gives.
Drift averages out over the twenty repeats instead, and the time
stamps let it be seen.

now: The top of the box is 1.95 V, not 1.98. The three voltages are
why: 1.98 V is 30 mV past the 0 to 1.95 V SkyWater gives for the gate
and drain of its 1.8 V devices, and past the fastest library
corner, ff_n40C_1v95. Found on 23 September.
gives_up: the box is no longer plus and minus ten percent about 1.80 V.

not_amended: The pairing, the bit convention, the exclusions and the refusal to drop outliers, the abstention rule read from extraction/TOLERANCES.json, the temperatures, the windows, the 20 repeats and the must_record list all stand as frozen.
preregister.py P10 still reads the frozen box, 1.62 to 1.98 V, and passes on it. The amended box is held by --amendment instead.
still_open: Whether the secondary named on 3 October gets an interval, and which.
The number of shuffles and the seed for M2's p-value, now that M2 is secondary.
E.3, the collector that has to read in this order, is not written. firmware/measure_puf.py is the bench script that already does, and it is not that collector.
The paper's preregistration section describes the frozen file. It takes this up in Phase C, with the sentence above.
